The present suit is filed by the plaintiff for the following reliefs:
a) To restrain the defendant, their agents, representatives, executives,
administrators, or any person or persons under them, from interfering by way of illegal methods with the plaintiff's peaceful possession and enjoyment of the schedule property.
b) To pass such other suitable orders as this Court may deem fit in the circumstances of the case, in the ends of justice, and to award costs of the suit.
2.
In the plaint the plaintiff has contended that, he is the owner of the suit property and has acquired the same through a sale deed.

3. It is further submitted that originally the suit property belonged to the plaintiff's vendor Society,
which got acquired an extent of 176.03 acres of land of Nagavara Village, Kasaba Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk, under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, through the Government of Karnataka under Notification No. RD 183 ABQ 82 dated 21/02/1986 and published in the Official Gazette dated 24/02/1986 in various Sy. numbers as detailed in the Gazette notification.
4. The plaintiff, being a member of the Society, applied for allotment of a site in the layout formed by the Society as per the layout plan sanctioned by the BDA.
The Committee of Management of the Society considered the application of the plaintiff, who was eligible for allotment of a site.
Accordingly, a site bearing BDA Site No. 409 in the layout was allotted, which is the schedule property.
5. It is further submitted that the plaintiff's vendor Society gave a possession certificate on 29/06/2009 and thereafter executed a registered sale deed.
As on the date of registration, the plaintiff is in possession and enjoyment of the suit property.
6. After the plaintiff purchased the suit schedule property, he applied for transfer of khata at BDA/BBMP.
The same was transferred in his name, and he has paid up-to-date tax to the concerned authority.

Sumanth A vs Murali P on 25 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193846283/
2
7. Now, this property is within BBMP, Bangalore, and he has paid up-to-date tax to BBMP and is in possession and enjoyment of the same.
The plaintiff is intending to construct a residential building and obtained the plan from the concerned authority, and the same was started with foundation work.
8. When the matter stood thus, the defendants, who are total strangers to the property, created bogus documents to grab money from the plaintiff.
The defendants are not related to the property.
They have local persons, money, and political influence in the locality.
The plaintiff has no support in the locality.
He is a private employee residing at Ganga Nagar, far from the suit property.
9. The defendants, with an intention to grab money, started to create galata in the suit property during the absence of the plaintiff.
The defendants tried to interfere with the property.

Taking advantage of the plaintiff's helplessness, on 11/07/2018 at about 10 AM, along with 10 to 15 supporters, they came near the schedule property without having any right, title, or interest over the same and quarreled with the plaintiff with an intention to grab the property.
The defendants, having no manner of title, started to construct a building on the suit property.
10. The illegal acts of the defendants and their persons were stopped by the plaintiff with the assistance of local neighbors.
The defendants returned with threats to come back again on 13/07/2018 and 14/07/2018 at 11 AM and proceeded to interfere with and stop the construction work.
11. The plaintiff complained about the illegal acts of the defendants to the jurisdictional police.
The police, instead of taking action against the defendants, advised them not to interfere in the property again.
However, the defendants again tried to interfere with the plaintiff's peaceful possession and enjoyment.
Thereafter, he lodged a complaint with the police, but the police directed him to approach the civil court.
12. Hence, the plaintiff, having no alternative, has approached this Court for the said relief.
13. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 have appeared in person pursuant to the summons and have filed a detailed written statement by denying and disputing the plaint averments.

In the written statement,
it is contended that the suit is not at all sustainable in law, facts, probabilities, and circumstances of the case on hand, and hence liable to be dismissed.

14. The suit of the plaintiff is bad for misjoinder and non-joinder of proper and necessary parties,
and on that ground alone, the same is liable to be rejected.
15. The suit schedule property is the property of the first and second defendants in view of the order passed by the Supreme Court of India.
16. The plaintiff, instead of seeking declaration and consequential relief, has sought only permanent injunction; hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed.

3 17.
The suit property is not in existence.
The alleged acquisition of land and formation of residential layout are not within the personal knowledge of the defendants.

The acquisition proceedings came to be canceled by the Supreme Court of India in proceedings initiated by the owners of the lands in question, and in the said order, the Supreme Court of India has also held that the sale transactions that took place in respect of the said lands were declared as null and void.
18. The said fact is within the knowledge of the plaintiff, and in spite of knowing the same, the plaintiff has filed the present suit by making an illusory theory for reasons best known to him.
The plaintiff and the Society, colluding with each other, have created the sale deed only to harass the true and lawful owner of the property and nothing else.

19. The plaintiff has approached BBMP on the basis of forged and fabricated documents and obtained entries in his favour without following any procedure as required under law; hence, the same are not binding on the defendants.

20. It is further submitted by the defendants that they are law-abiding and peace-loving citizens,
and have no support of any men or material as alleged by the plaintiff.

On the other hand, the plaintiff himself is a more powerful and influential person in the area, having political power to achieve his illegal object, and accordingly, he has filed the above suit only to harass the defendants and nothing else, with an intention of grabbing the valuable property of the defendants.
21. It is further submitted that at no point of time did the defendants interfere with the possession of the property of the plaintiff.

On the other hand, the plaintiff, along with antisocial elements, has been interfering with the possession and enjoyment of the property of the defendants in one way or the other, for reasons best known to him.
22. The plaintiff and his antisocial elements alone are often interfering with the possession and enjoyment of the property of these defendants.

In this regard, the defendants resisted their illegal and high- handed acts with the support of family members and also lodged a complaint before the police authorities, but the police, hand in glove with the plaintiff, failed to render any protection to the defendants and, on the other hand, advised that the matter is of civil nature and thereby were unable to interfere with the matter.

23. It is submitted that the Bangalore Development Authority has issued a notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, whereby the State Government/BDA proposed the acquisition of 165 acres and 31 guntas of land of Nagavara and other surrounding villages along with the land of the defendants for the purpose of formation of a residential layout.

24. Thereafter, the said Bangalore Development Authority, in active collusion with the officials of the Vyalikaval House Building Cooperative Society, handed over possession of the property, acting detrimental to the very purpose of acquisition of the property.
Some of the landowners filed writ petitions for quashing the notification, contending that the acquisition was not for a public purpose.

4 25.

Further, finally, the Supreme Court of India, in Civil Appeal No. 1930 of 2012 arising out of SLP (Civil) No. 24972/2002, directed the Vyalikaval House Building Cooperative Society Limited to return the land to the concerned landowners within a period of two months from the date of the order.

26. In view of the Supreme Court of India's order in the above-mentioned proceedings, the defendants did re pay the award amount that was collected by them.

Accordingly, the property was restored to the original owners of the lands, and further, the Special Tahsildar issued the mutation (RTC) in RRT(D) CR 6/21/2010-11 dated 01/04/2011, restoring khata, since the defendants were in possession.

27. Later, the defendants, by consent of all the family members, gifted the entire property, and accordingly, the defendants are in possession and enjoyment of the same as true and lawful owners,
enjoying the same by paying property tax, etc., as per dues to the concerned authorities.

28. It is further submitted that the plaintiff, being a stranger to the suit property, might have created some documents and filed the false and frivolous suit with an intention to knock off the valuable property.

If the contention taken by the plaintiff is to be believed, then he has to file a suit for declaration along with permanent injunction and has to prove his ownership, title, and interest over the property.
In the absence of the same, the suit is liable to be rejected.

29. It is further contended that the property bearing Sy. No. 34/1 of Nagawara Village, Bangalore North Taluk, measuring 1 acre including 14 guntas of kara land, is an ancestral property of Appaji @
Appajappa, constituting a Hindu undivided family.

He had 3 sons, i.e., Krishnappa, Shri Narayana,
and Shri Muniyappa.
Appajappa, during his lifetime, succeeded to the above properties.
After his demise, Shri Krishnappa, his eldest son, succeeded to the said property.

30. The Bangalore Development Authority, by notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, proposed to acquire 165 acres and 30 guntas of land of Nagawara Village and other surrounding areas, along with this schedule property, for the benefit of Vyalikaval House Building Cooperative Society Limited.

sentences.text: Thereafter, by notification under Section 6(1), the Bangalore Development Authority took possession of the entire land by distributing compensation to the landowners.

31. Aggrieved by the acquisition, some of the landowners filed petitions before the High Court of Karnataka for quashing the notification, contending that the acquisition was not for a public purpose.
Thereafter, they filed Special Leave Petitions before the Supreme Court of India in Civil Appeal No. 1930 of 2012.
The Supreme Court directed Vyalikaval House Building Cooperative Society Limited to return the lands to the concerned landowners within a period of 2 months from the date of the order.

In view of the order of the Supreme Court, Muniratnamma, grandmother of Smt. Venkatamma,
refunded the amount of 98,306 to the concerned Special Land Acquisition Officer, Bangalore.

The said officer, as per the Government Order, accepted the refund amount and restored the ownership and possession of the landed property bearing Sy. No. 34/1 of Nagawara Village, measuring 1 acre and 14 guntas, to the original owner, Smt. Venkatamma, W/o Krishnappa.

33. After restoration of ownership and possession of the said property to Smt. Venkatamma, the Special Land Acquisition Officer issued a 'Subardu Patra' dated 25/06/2009, bearing LAC No. 409 of 1985-86, confirming the restoration of ownership and possession of the land to the said Venkatamma.
The same was notified to the revenue authorities to restore khata in the name of the above landowner, Smt. Venkatamma.

Accordingly, all revenue documents were restored in the name of Smt. Venkatamma, and hence, she enjoyed possession of the land having absolute right, title,
interest, and ownership.
34. It is further submitted by the defendant that, out of love and affection, Smt. Venkatamma gifted the property to her granddaughter, Smt. Muniratnamma, through a gift deed dated 01-10-2014.
Accordingly, Muniratnamma was put in possession of the said landed property bearing Sy. No. 34/1 of Nagawara Village, Kasba Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk, measuring 1 acre 8 guntas.

Thereafter,
she enjoyed the possession of the said property peacefully by getting the mutation and RTC changed to her name.

35. It is further submitted that, by virtue of the gift deed dated 01-10-2014, she held and enjoyed possession of the property without any disturbance till 07-07-2017, i.e., the date of sale of the said property to defendant Nos. 1 and 2 herein.

The defendant Nos. 1 and 2, after enquiry and careful examination of possession and documents, purchased the above said property, viz.:
(a) The defendant No. 1 purchased a portion of the land with possession measuring 35,992 sq. ft., comprising land bearing Sy. No. 34/1 of Nagawara Village, Kasba Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk,
through a registered sale deed dated 07- 07-2017

. 
(b) The defendant No. 2 purchased the remaining portion of land measuring 10,000 sq. ft.,
comprising land in Sy. No. 34/1 of Nagawara Village, Kasba Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk, through a registered sale deed dated 07-07-2017.
36.

It is further submitted that, after the sale in favour of defendant Nos. 1 and 2, they were put in possession of their respective portions of land bearing Sy. No. 34/1 of Nagawara Village, and defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are presently in possession of the said property.
Recently, defendant Nos. 1 and 2 came to know about the suit, and immediately they made a detailed enquiry about the plaintiff.
It is learnt that, before filing of the suit, the plaintiff had created certain sale documents.
Thereafter, the defendants have filed a criminal complaint, which is pending enquiry before the jurisdictional police.

That, knowing fully well about the ownership and possession of Smt. Venkatamma and Muniratnamma, along with others, some persons filed civil suits individually, and she contested all the said suits.
The suits were dismissed for failure to prove possession over the respective suit properties.

38. That the transaction between Kenchappa and the children of Appaji and Muniyappa, in respect of the entire extent of 1 acre 8 guntas of land in Sy. No. 34/1 of Nagawara Village, under a registered sale deed dated 20-05-2003, is a void sale deed.
At the time of execution of the sale deed in favour of Kariyappa by the children of late Appaji and Sri Muniyappa, the said property had already been acquired by the Government.
Hence, the BDA was the owner of the property, and possession of the land was with the BDA.
39. The plaintiff, while filing the injunction suit, has to keep in mind that a suit for injunction without seeking declaratory relief is not maintainable.
He ought to have sought declaration and injunction; hence, the suit filed by the plaintiff is not maintainable.
The suit is also not maintainable for non-joinder of necessary parties.
40. It is further submitted that the suit property is physically non-existent, and only on the basis of alleged documents relied upon by the plaintiff, the suit is filed.
Presently, defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the land bearing Sy. No. 34/1 of Nagawara Village, Kasba Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk.
41. The plaintiff is an influential person in the society, making hectic efforts to interfere with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 over the property.
There is no cause of action to file the suit against the defendants, and the alleged cause of action is imaginary and created only for the purpose of filing the suit.
42. The plaintiff has filed the suit by suppressing true facts.
Defendant No. 2 and others have filed a suit for the relief of declaration and injunction in O.S. No. 1144 of 2020 in respect of Sy. No. 34 situated at Nagawara Village.

Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 have sought the relief of declaration in respect of Sy. No. 34/1, and further sought judgment and decree declaring that the sale deed dated 20-05-2003 executed in favour of Kariyappa is void, and consequently sought cancellation of the same.
They have further sought to declare themselves as absolute owners in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the property bearing Sy. No. 34/1 situated at Nagawara Village.

43. The suit filed by defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in O.S. No. 1144 of 2020 is pending before this Court,
and the plaintiffs have been made parties to the said suit by filing an impleading application.
The plaintiff is also claiming title in respect of Site No. 409 in the same Sy. No., including Sy. No. 34/1 situated at Nagawara Village, without having any right over the suit property.
The plaintiffs have filed a false suit before this Court to harass these defendants in one way or the other.
The plaintiffs have not come to the Court with clean hands, and under these circumstances, the plaintiff is not entitled to any relief.

52.

The plaintiff has approached this Court seeking the relief of permanent injunction to restrain the defendants, their agents, representatives, servants, or any person Sumanth A vs Murali P on 25 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193846283/
9 claiming under them, from interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property by the plaintiff, along with such other reliefs.
53. In the plaint, the plaintiff has contended that he is the absolute owner in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property.

It is further contended that the Government acquired an extent of 176.03 acres of land situated in Nagawara Village, Kasaba Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk, under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, vide Notification No. RD 183 AQB 82 dated 21-02-1986, for the purpose of formation of a layout by the Vyalikaval House Building Co-operative Society Limited, Bangalore.

The said layout was approved by the Bangalore Development Authority vide Resolution No. 156/2003 dated 12-09-2003, and Work Order bearing No. BDA/TPM/PL/32/1685/2003-04 dated 30-09- 2003.
54.
The plaintiff further contends that he is a member of the said Society and had applied for allotment of a site.
Accordingly, the suit schedule property, i.e., Site No. 409 formed in the said layout, was allotted to him.
A possession certificate was issued in his favour on 29-06-2009, and a registered sale deed was executed on 30-06-2009 by the said Society.
Since then, the plaintiff claims to be in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property as its absolute owner.
55. It is further contended that the defendants have no manner of right, title, or interest over the suit schedule property.
However, they attempted to interfere with the plaintiff's possession on 11-07-2018 and thereafter made attempts to dispossess him.
The plaintiff lodged a complaint before the jurisdictional police; however, he was advised to approach the competent civil court.
Hence, the present suit is filed.
56. Per contra, the defendants, who have appeared through counsel, have filed their written statement denying and disputing the plaint averments.
It is contended that the suit schedule property itself is not in existence.

It is further contended that the preliminary notification issued under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, for acquisition of lands in Nagawara and surrounding areas for formation of a residential layout by the said Society was challenged by certain landowners.

57. It is further contended that in Civil Appeal No. 1930/2012 before the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, the acquisition proceedings were set aside, and the Society was directed to restore the lands to the original landowners within two months from the date of the order.
It was also directed that the compensation paid be recovered from the beneficiaries.
Accordingly, the lands were restored to the original landowners.
58. The defendants further contend that land bearing Sy. No. 34/1 of Nagawara Village, measuring 1 acre 2 guntas (including 14 guntas of kharab), originally belonged to one Appaji @ Appajjappa.
He had three sons, namely Krishnappa, Narayana, and Muniyappa, who succeeded to the said property in a family partition.

It is further contended that the land acquired for the formation of layout was restored to Venkatamma upon refund of compensation amounting to 98,326/- to the Government.

Thereafter,
the khata was restored in the name of the original landowners.

Subsequently, the khata stood in the name of Venkatamma, wife of Krishnappa, and possession was restored by the Government by issuing a "Subardu patra".
60.

It is further contended that the said Venkatamma executed a registered gift deed dated 01- 10-2014 in favour of her granddaughter Munirathnamma, conveying land measuring 1 acre 8 guntas in Sy. No. 34/1 of Nagawara Village.

Thereafter, said Munirathanamma and her family members sold portions of the property, measuring 35,992 sq. ft. in favour of Defendant No. 1 and 10,000 sq.
ft. in favour of Defendant No. 2 under registered sale deeds dated 07- 07-2017.
61.
Since then, the defendants claim to be in lawful possession and enjoyment of the said property as absolute owners.
It is their contention that the plaintiff is falsely claiming rights over the property despite the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court setting aside the acquisition proceedings.

Hence, the defendants have prayed for dismissal of the suit.
62.

The plaintiff, in the present suit, seeks a decree of permanent injunction against the defendants,
basing his claim on title.
Therefore, the burden squarely lies upon the plaintiff to establish lawful title and possession over the suit schedule property as on the date of the suit.

63. In this regard, the plaintiff has produced the original sale deed marked as Ex.P.3, executed by Vyalikaval House Building Cooperative Society Limited in his favour on 29.06.2009, pertaining to the suit schedule property.

sentences.text: The plaintiff has also produced the possession certificate issued by the said society, marked as Ex.P.2, dated 29.06.2009.
Further, the plaintiff has produced the rectification deed dated 28.07.2016, marked as Ex.P.4, whereby the boundaries of the suit schedule property were rectified.
64. The remaining revenue documents, namely tax paid receipts, khatha registration, and building license, do not, by themselves, confer or establish title over the property.
Hence, they are not material for adjudication of title and possession of the suit schedule property.
